In '''mathematical''' group theory, the '''balance theorem''' states that if ''G'' is a group with no [[core (group)|core]], then ''G'' either has disconnected [[Sylow subgroup|Sylow 2-subgroups]], or it is of [[characteristic 2 type]], or it is of component type {{harv|Gorenstein|1983|p=7 }}.

The significance of this theorem is that it splits the [[classification of finite simple groups]] into three major subcases.
